routes.name: Certificate of Residence (Due to Long stay)

note: Uganda, read on the Directorate of Citizenship and Immigration Control's own pages (immigration.go.ug) on 2026-10-30; its fees are stated in US dollars, so the file's currency is USD. Work on a short contract takes the Special Pass, applied for online through the Immigration Portal with the contract and the engaging company's covering letter (either: the page doesn't say from where), US$400 for 3 months; the work is the contract's (work for the sponsor). A work permit 'allows the applicant to live and work in Uganda' and is always sponsored by an organisation with an organisation code; a salaried expatriate's is Entry Permit Class G2: US$1,250 for 6 months, US$2,500 for 12 (kept), US$5,000 for 24 and US$7,500 for 36, each over 6 months including a non-refundable US$1,500. Nationals of Kenya and Rwanda pay no immigration fees but still need the permit; Tanzanians pay US$1,550 a year (the form keeps one fee). A Certificate of Residence 'due to long stay' is for one who has lived in Uganda continuously for 10 years and contributed to its socio-economic development (10 kept as the work permit's years to it), US$4,000 for 5 years, US$3,500 for 10 and US$3,000 for life including a US$200 processing fee, as the page states them; the life certificate is kept as the permanent route, its holder read as free to work. It is read as applied for in Uganda, since it asks ten years' stay there. Decision times and naturalisation's years aren't on the pages.

sources.title: DCIC Uganda, Special Pass
sources.said: This is a temporary pass that allows one to work on short contract, obtain medical treatment, tourism and exploring business opportunities etc. ... available online through the ... Copy of Contract ... USD 400 for 3 months

sources.title: DCIC Uganda, Work Permit
sources.said: This permit allows the applicant to live and work in Uganda. This permit is always sponsored by an organization or company which must have a mandatory organization code.

sources.title: DCIC Uganda, Entry Permit
sources.said: issued to foreign expatriates employed in Uganda including salaried employees working in NGOs ... Nationals from Kenya and Rwanda are exempted from payment of immigration fees however, they should apply and obtain the work permit ... For nationals from Tanzania, the work permit fees have been revised to USD 1550 per year.

sources.title: DCIC Uganda, Class G2
sources.said: 6 Months cost USD 1250 ... 12 Months, cost USD 2500 (including a $1500 non-refundable fee) ... 24 Months, cost USD 5000 (including a $1500 non-refundable fee) ... 36 Months, cost USD 7500 (including a $1500 non-refundable fee)

sources.title: DCIC Uganda, Certificate of Residence: Due to Long stay
sources.said: this is issued to a person that has continuously lived in the country for 10 years and has contributed to the socio-economic development of Uganda ... For 5 years pay USD 4,000 ... For 10 years pay USD 3,500 ... For Life pay USD 3,000 (including a $200 processing fee)
